# creditcardforgiveness.org

> Free guide to credit card debt forgiveness, settlement, hardship programs, and bankruptcy discharge.

creditcardforgiveness.org is a free, open-source educational resource about credit card debt relief options -- what "forgiveness" really means, how settlement works, bank hardship programs, bankruptcy discharge, tax implications, and how to avoid scams. Part of the Open Bankruptcy Project.

## Pages

- https://creditcardforgiveness.org/: Main guide to credit card debt forgiveness -- what it really is, how it works, and your real options.
- https://creditcardforgiveness.org/settlement-vs-bankruptcy.html: Detailed comparison of debt settlement versus bankruptcy filing for credit card debt.
- https://creditcardforgiveness.org/tax-implications.html: 1099-C cancellation of debt income -- the tax trap most people miss when settling credit card debt.
- https://creditcardforgiveness.org/hardship-programs.html: Bank hardship programs explained -- what they offer, how to qualify, and what to watch out for.
- https://creditcardforgiveness.org/scams.html: How to spot credit card debt forgiveness scams -- red flags, common tactics, and legitimate alternatives.
- https://creditcardforgiveness.org/chapter-7.html: How Chapter 7 bankruptcy discharges credit card debt completely with no tax consequences.
- https://creditcardforgiveness.org/chapter-13.html: How Chapter 13 bankruptcy handles credit card debt through a repayment plan.
- https://creditcardforgiveness.org/how-much-debt.html: How much credit card debt makes forgiveness, settlement, or bankruptcy worth pursuing.
- https://creditcardforgiveness.org/faq.html: Frequently asked questions about credit card debt forgiveness, settlement, and bankruptcy.

## Key Facts

- "Credit card forgiveness" is not a government program -- it usually means settlement, hardship programs, or bankruptcy discharge
- Debt settlement typically requires paying 40-60% of the balance in a lump sum
- Settled or forgiven debt over $600 triggers a 1099-C and is taxable as income (IRC Section 61)
- Bankruptcy discharge under 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a) eliminates credit card debt with no tax consequences
- The insolvency exception (IRC Section 108) can reduce or eliminate the tax on cancelled debt
- Bank hardship programs may reduce interest rates or monthly payments but rarely reduce principal
- Debt settlement companies charge 15-25% of enrolled debt and have high failure rates
- Chapter 7 eliminates credit card debt entirely in 3-4 months if you qualify under the means test
- Chapter 13 lets you pay what you can afford over 3-5 years, then discharges the rest
